questions.stem: Which site of the Indus Valley Civilization is famous for having an artificial brick dockyard, proving its role as a major maritime trade center?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Lothal (located in modern-day Gujarat near the Gulf of Khambhat) is one of the most prominent IVC sites. It is unique for possessing what archaeologists believe is the world's earliest known artificial dockyard, connecting the city to the ancient course of the Sabarmati river. It was a thriving trade center exporting beads, gems, and ornaments to West Asia and Africa.
DECOY BUSTING: Mohenjo-daro is famous for the Great Bath and the Dancing Girl bronze statue. Harappa was the first site discovered (giving the civilization its name). Kalibangan (Rajasthan) is famous for its 'ploughed field' and fire altars.
EXAM INSIGHT: Lothal was excavated by S.R. Rao in 1954. It is also unique among IVC sites because its houses had entrances on the main street, unlike other IVC cities where entrances were deliberately placed in side-alleys.

questions.stem: The UNESCO World Heritage site of Dholavira, a major Harappan city, is globally recognized for which of its unique architectural features?

options.option_text: A highly sophisticated water conservation and harvesting system
The largest granary ever found in the Indus Valley Civilization
Evidence of the earliest known iron-smelting furnaces
A massive circular amphitheater used for religious ceremonies

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Dholavira (located on Khadir Bet island in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat) is renowned for its extraordinarily sophisticated water management system. Because it was located in an arid region with no perennial rivers, the inhabitants built a series of massive stone reservoirs and check dams to harvest and store rainwater. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Great Granary was found at Mohenjo-daro/Harappa. The Harappans did NOT know iron (they were a Bronze Age civilization, iron came much later in the Vedic period). They did not build amphitheaters.
EXAM INSIGHT: Dholavira is also structurally unique. Most Harappan cities were divided into two parts (a raised Citadel and a Lower Town). Dholavira, however, was divided into THREE principal divisions: the Citadel, a Middle Town, and a Lower Town. It recently received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2021.

questions.stem: Which prominent Indus Valley site, located on the banks of the Ghaggar river in Rajasthan, yielded evidence of both pre-Harappan and mature Harappan phases, as well as distinct 'fire altars'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kalibangan (meaning 'black bangles') is located in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. It is a highly significant site because it shows evidence of a ploughed agricultural field dating back to the PRE-Harappan period. It also features several raised brick platforms containing 'fire altars', suggesting ritualistic fire sacrifices.
DECOY BUSTING: Banawali (Haryana) is famous for a terracotta model of a plough. Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is currently believed to be the largest IVC site in the Indian subcontinent. Surkotada (Gujarat) is the only IVC site that has yielded the controversial remains of horse bones.
EXAM INSIGHT: The presence of fire altars in Kalibangan and Lothal suggests regional variations in religious practices, as these are absent in the major cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
